A1.justification: Both complete, readable 18-page PDFs describe HieraMamba by the same authors. Text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material support comparison; relocated and renumbered content can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original grounding experiments on Ego4D-NLQ, MAD-v1/v2 and TACoS, alongside efficiency measurements, ablations and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Mamba-based comparisons, parameter sweeps, additional loss ablations and qualitative failure cases.

M1.justification: The proposed AMP hierarchy, global Hydra and local Transformer encoders, gates, ACC/SPC objectives and decoding procedure are retained. Rewritten explanations do not establish an algorithm change; the newly evaluated Mamba adaptations are comparison models.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Ego4D-NLQ, MAD-v1/v2 and TACoS grounding coverage. Additional loss ablations reuse these datasets, and the new failure examples examine cases within existing Ego4D coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds VideoMamba+SnAG and SnAG-Mamba in a targeted Ego4D comparison with SnAG and HieraMamba (Table 5). These directly test simple SSM adaptations. Comparator membership in the existing benchmark tables and efficiency comparison remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 and Table 3 change the stated MAD-v1 features from CLIP ViT-L/14 to ViT-B/32; unchanged scores do not establish whether experiments were rerun. New protocols independently sweep loss coefficients and test 2, 4, 8 and 10 AMP layers. Existing splits and recall metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond retained component and pooling ablations, v2 tests simple Mamba substitutions, loss-weight sensitivity and depth/parameter trade-offs (Tables 5, 8–9). Supplementary Table 12 adds MAD-v2 and TACoS loss ablations, and Section 3.3/Figure 7 introduce six failure cases. These substantially expand diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Both supplementary Section 1 introductions state that results are averaged over five runs. v2 adds no new seed information, uncertainty intervals, error bars or significance-testing practice. Additional result rows do not establish increased repetition.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial diagnostic results: Table 5 reports 12.44 for VideoMamba+SnAG and 22.88 for SnAG-Mamba versus 25.66 for HieraMamba; Tables 8–9 and 12 add sensitivity and cross-dataset loss results, alongside failure outcomes. Existing HieraMamba headline scores remain unchanged. Table 4 changes DeCafNet's TACoS R@5 at IoU 0.3 from 81.15 to 81.05 while retaining its 64.11 average.

T1.justification: Section 4.3.1 removes v1's conflicting floor-based anchor count and uses L1, already defined using a ceiling in Section 4.3. Section 4.4 also removes the explicit SPC positive-set definition while retaining that set in Equation 6. The substantive SSM and loss equations otherwise remain, with no new proofs.

C1.justification: v2's introduction newly claims HieraMamba is the first hierarchical state-space video model for temporal grounding in hour-long videos. The central AMP/contrastive-learning contributions and state-of-the-art claims on the same three benchmarks are retained.

C2.justification: New failure discussion identifies visibility/action confusion, object misidentification, occlusion sensitivity and difficulties with noncanonical views, extending beyond the retained frozen-backbone and fixed-stride limitations. Section 5.5 newly argues that generic SSM substitution is insufficient and attributes gains to AMP. Section 5.3 also broadens the interpretation of recall gains beyond boundary tightening.

D1.justification: v2 revises the MAD feature specification and documents coefficient grids, depth configurations and parameter counts. Supplementary implementation, decoding, training hyperparameters and code-access statements remain essentially unchanged. Conversely, the SPC description drops v1's explicit statement that segment pooling uses the mean.

R1.justification: The same 80 referenced works are retained. Positioning changes through the new first-of-its-kind claim and the explicit empirical distinction between HieraMamba and straightforward VideoMamba/Hydra adaptations; the broader related-work coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively edited and condensed across the abstract, introduction, related work, architecture/loss explanations, results discussion and conclusion. Section 5.5 is reorganized around additional controls and sweeps, and acknowledgements are added. This is a broad editorial revision despite retaining the principal section sequence.

P2.justification: v2 restyles Figures 1–2, arranges Tables 2–4 side by side, removes Table 2's venue column and packs several diagnostic tables together. The full Ego4D loss breakdown moves into expanded supplementary Table 12. A failure figure is added, while the former Figure 7 is retained as Figure 8. The resulting layout is substantially denser.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through direct Mamba controls, sensitivity tests and documented cross-dataset loss effects, while adding useful failure analysis absent from v1. These improve support and transparency. The net gain is tempered by limited setup detail for the new controls, omitted SPC details, denser tables and the changed DeCafNet entry whose retained average no longer matches its four scores.
